artifacts.summary: Maps every archive/vault hand-rolled state.json write site in file_scope, flags a fresh-create design fork state-write.sh cannot cover with a plain flag, and names out-of-scope sites (archive-task.sh, vault-operation.sh, jq-escaping-workarounds.md, review.md, extension-domain debt) that will affect the verification bar.

memory_candidates.content: When generalizing a single-file mutex-guarded writer (like state-write.sh) to cover additional target files (archive/vault state.json), keep the underlying mutex (specs/.scope-lock) a single global lock rather than per-file. Per-file locks create a real ABBA deadlock risk when a single logical operation interleaves writes to two different target files in different orders across concurrent callers (e.g. recover: archive-then-live vs abandon: live-then-archive-then-live). A single lock makes every acquire/release pair sequential and non-nested regardless of target file, at negligible serialization cost for rare, human/agent-paced operations.

A jq-filter-based read-modify-write helper (state-write.sh style: `jq $FILTER $EXISTING_FILE`) cannot express a fresh-file-create operation (`jq -n '{...}' > newfile`, no existing input) without an explicit no-input/init mode, because its contract assumes the target file already exists. Before assuming a generic '--target-file' flag closes every hand-rolled write site, check whether each site is actually a transform-of-existing-file vs a create-from-scratch -- the latter needs a distinct code path.
